chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the slaughtered meat of the Dhimmi (non-Muslim subject), so he said: 'Do not eat it if he named [God], and if he did not name [God] [do not eat it].'

key_terms.الذِّمِّيِّ: Dhimmi (non-Muslim subject living under Islamic protection)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating meat slaughtered by a Dhimmi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that the meat of a Dhimmi is not to be eaten, regardless of whether they recited God's name during slaughter or not. This indicates a stricter standard for Dhimmi slaughter compared to some other views that accept it if the name is mentioned. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is often cited to support the view that the mere profession of Islam or status of Dhimmi is insufficient for their slaughter to be Halal unless they are specifically recognized as 'People of the Book' (Ahl al-Kitab) and follow their own ritual laws, distinguishing them from polytheists whose slaughter is explicitly prohibited.
